A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LogicXGNN work, with 32 readable pages including Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons localize the differences to Figure 2 and the arXiv version/date stamp; the remaining material matches.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments measuring explanation fidelity, runtime, coverage, stability, and validity in Section 4, with additional results and examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–4 and supplementary evaluations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Predicate construction, decision-tree rule extraction, orbit-based grounding, and inference remain unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices. The revised overview diagram depicts the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same molecular, synthetic, and social graph datasets, including the three large-scale benchmarks. The continuous-feature demonstration using modified Mutagenicity data in Appendix D.3 is also retained.

E2.justification: GLGExplainer and GraphTrail retain the same participation in the reported comparisons. The baseline exclusions, reproduction procedures, and architecture comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: The 80/20 splits, GNN configurations, training settings, evaluation metrics, explanation-complexity controls, and time limits match. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The tree-depth analysis in Figure 3, grounding-failure analyses, stability evaluation, synthetic-rule recovery, and appendix examples are unchanged. Figure 2 redraws the existing methodological illustration rather than adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-seed evaluation practice and identical uncertainty reporting. Appendix B.1 retains the explanation that seeds affect the entire pipeline, including GNN training.

E6.justification: Reported experimental values and findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains LogicXGNN's BBBP fidelity of 85.32 ± 2.96%. Figure 2 retains the same graph-level values, activation matrix, and resulting rules.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, complexity analysis, Algorithm 1, and Theorem D.1 with its proof are unchanged. The diagram revision introduces no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same grounding contribution and claims of over 20% average fidelity improvement and 10–100× speedup. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of baseline grounding failures, architectural applicability, continuous-feature handling, and explanation utility match. Existing qualifications, including the omitted NCI1 visual examples and rationale against a human study, are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information remains identical, including hardware, optimizer settings, CART usage, baseline matching procedures, and code access. The schematic redraw does not revise implementation instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to local, global rule-based, and self-explainable GNN approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are limited to labels within Figure 2 and the arXiv version/date stamp. Main prose, captions, section ordering, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2(a) is redrawn: numeric node identifiers and degree annotations give way to A/B node labels, explicit embedding vectors become shaded blocks, and predicate examples receive revised styling. The same workflow remains, with no substantive changes to other figures, tables, or page layout.

improvement.justification: The redesigned Figure 2(a) is less crowded and makes node types easier to see. However, it removes explicit node embedding values and numeric node identifiers, while Section 3.3 still uses those identifiers to explain subgraph features and predicate training examples. With the scientific content unchanged, the readability gains and reduced traceability do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
